Hon'ble Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal,J.
1.

Heard Sri Abhishek Tripathi, learned counsel holding brief of Sri Rehan Waris, learned counsel
for the applicant and Sri Ramesh Kumar, learned Aga for the State.

2.  The present 482 Cr.P.C. application has been filed to quash the entire proceedings of Complaint Case No.590 of 2023 (Smt. Kusum Yadav Vs. Shaili Verma), under Section-138 of Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act, 1881'), Police Station-Railway Road,
District-Meerut, pending in the court of learned Judicial Magistrate, Meerut as well as impugned order dated 30.05.2024 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Court No.11, Meerut in Criminal Revision No.219 of 2023 as well as impugned order dated 02.03.2023 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate, Court No.3, Meerut.

sentences.text: 3. Contention of learned counsel for the applicant is that cheque in question was forcibly taken by the complainant from his shop.

To that regard, the applicant had also filed a complaint on Shaili Verma vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100005245/
1 20.02.2023, u/s 307, 389, 452, 420, 504, 506 IPC and Section 25 of Arms Act, 1959 before the court of ACJ (Senior Division), Court No.7, Meerut.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, no case u/s 138 of the Act, 1881 is made out against the applicant.

In support of his contention learned counsel for the applicant has also relied upon the judgement of the Apex Court in the case of Raj Kumar Khurana Vs. State of (NCT of Delhi) & Anr in Criminal Appeal No.913 of 2009 in which Apex Court observed that when the FIR was lodged regarding missing of cheque and subsequently cheque was presented and same was returned with the endorsement 'payment stopped' then no liability u/s 138 of the Act, 1881 will be attracted.

entities.text: Raj Kumar Khurana Vs. State of (NCT of Delhi) & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. Per contra, learned AGA has submitted that in the present case after filing of the complaint by the opposite party no.2 on 12.01.2023, the present applicant had filed a complaint on 20.02.2023 just to create the defence.

5. After hearing the rival contention of learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of record, it appears that on bouncing of the cheque alleged to be issued by the applicant to opposite party no.2,
complaint was filed by the opposite party no.2 on 12.01.2023, u/s 138 of the Act, 1881, when despite the demand notice, cheque amount was not paid by the applicant and thereafter present applicant also filed a complaint dated 20.02.2023 mentioning that opposite party no.2 along with other family members came to the shop of the husband of the applicant and forcibly took cheque in question along with other documents.
Additionally, it is also clear from the record that cheque in question was returned by the bank for insufficiency of fund not for stopping the payment of cheque amount.
Therefore, the fact of the present case is totally different from the fact of the case of Raj Kumar Khurana (supra).
Therefore, that judgement will not help the applicant.
Even otherwise, the ground raised by the applicant is his defence and disputed question of fact that cannot be a ground to quash the impugned proceeding.
6. In view of the above, this court does not find any illegality in the impugned proceeding.
7. Therefore, present application is rejected.
